title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 3 of a typed draft with handwritten corrections. The whole page is struck through by diagonal lines, and the margin has question marks. It is not a manuscript note on cycles proper, and it is unrelated to the K-equivalence material on the neighbouring pages. It may be connected to the 1965 letter mentioned in the cote, but the image does not establish that.

Setting (all fibre products are over S):
- G is an S-group acting on an S-object V, and W ⊂ V is a sub-object.
- N is the stabilizer of W in G, i.e. the g with g·W = W.
- Z ⊂ G×V is the closed incidence subobject {(g,v) : g^{-1}v ∈ W}.
- X ⊂ G/N × V is its image {(gN, v) : v ∈ gW}. The pair (Z, X) sits in a cartesian square called (xx).
- For a point v, the transporter M_v(S') = {g ∈ G(S') : v ∈ g·W(S')} = {g : g^{-1}v ∈ W}. If v is a section of W, then N ⊂ M_v.

Representability:
- The constructions so far are purely functorial and work on any site.
- Now assume N is representable, faithfully flat and quasi-compact over S, and G/N is representable. Over a field with G of finite type this holds automatically; the text cites 'Exp VIII 6' and 'Exp VI', i.e. SGA 3.
- Then X is representable by fpqc descent. G×V → G/N×V is faithfully flat and quasi-compact, and Z is a closed subscheme of G×V stable under the right action of N, so Z descends to a closed subscheme X ⊂ G/N×V.
- Hence the diagram (D) is a diagram of preschemes over S.

Infinitesimal set-up (S = Spec k, G, V, W of finite type):
- Let n = Lie(N). Then dim N ≤ dim_k n, with equality iff N is smooth (SGA 3 Exp VI_A).
- For a ∈ W(k), M_a is a closed subscheme of G containing N and isomorphic to φ^{-1}(a). The map φ is defined on an earlier page and is not visible here.
- Let m_a be the Zariski tangent space of M_a at e. Then n ⊂ m_a and dim N ≤ dim n ≤ dim m_a.

Lemma 1.1 begins with condition (i): n = m_a and N smooth. The remaining conditions are on the next typed page, which is not in this folder sequence.

Purpose: this is the standard tangent-space comparison controlling whether the incidence correspondence X → V (or φ) is smooth or étale at a point, i.e. how a point lies on the translates g·W. Such statements underlie transversality and moving arguments for translates of a subvariety under a group action, which would explain why the draft sits in the cycles folder.
errors: The reference 'Exp VIII 6' for representability of G/N over a field is imprecise. In SGA 3 as published, quotients by subgroups over a field are in Exp VI_A, and smoothness via Lie algebra dimension is in Exp VI_A as well. This is probably due to a draft numbering of the exposés.
The definition of φ, and why M_a ≅ φ^{-1}(a) rather than M_a/N, is not visible on this page. It depends on how φ is defined earlier, so the claim cannot be checked here.
